newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says no one buys policy action from him.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says no one buys policy action from him.

text.p: President Bill Clinton acknowledged on Tuesday that he gives "a respectful hearing" to those who donate large sums to Democratic campaign coffers but added: "Nobody buys a guaranteed result."

"What they get from me, I think, is a respectful hearing if they have some concern about the issues ... but nobody buys a guaranteed result, nor should they ever," Clinton said at a news conference in which he pledged to support efforts to reform political fund-raising but also defended his own plans to attended a $1 million fund-raiser on Tuesday evening.

The White House has been under fire since last year's presidential election campaign for Democratic fund-raising practices that have raised eyebrows and will be subject to congressional and Justice Departmenbt hearings. Clinton said the need for reform was clear, adding, "Anyone who's involved in politics must accept responsibility for this problem and take responsiblity to repair it. That is true for me and true for others as well."

But he defended the need for political fund-raising generally, saying: "I don't think there is anything wrong with raising money for the political process. The problem is the volume of money, the amount of money, the time it takes to raise, the inevitable questions that are raised."

Critics have questioned whether the access huge contributions gives political donors does not amount to infuence peddling, but Clinton said some access is "a good thing when contributors care about the country and have some particular area of expertise they want to contribute."

Asked about a controversial episode in which banking industry officials had been invited to have coffee in the White House, he said they were legitimate as a venue for such exchanges of views but he conceded that it probably was not proper for federal banking regulators also to be present.
